title: Migration narrative contradicts the round-2 mint-at-save and tombstone fixes
evidence:
-- continue_token is 288 bits of URL-safe entropy (wisp.random_string(48)),
-- same capability model as application.erasure_token: the token IS the
-- auth. Partial unique index — most rows have NULL (token minted lazily on
-- the first "email me a link" request).
(and header line 12-13: "--   * Erasure — the continue email carries a self-service delete link
--     (POST /apply/:code/draft-erasure/:token) that removes the row.")
detail: W1 fix mints the token at every save (upsert_application_draft.sql: 'The continue token is minted at SAVE time'), so 'most rows have NULL / minted lazily' is now false; erasure tombstones (erased_at) rather than 'removes the row'. Stale schema narrative misleads future readers of the only durable design doc.
recommended_fix: Author a comment-only follow-up migration (or update the header text pre-merge) stating tokens are minted at save time and erasure is a tombstone retained until vacancy close.

title: Stage-2 reminder continue-link (tokenized capability URL) built from request origin, against the PR's own B1 principle
evidence:
Ok(token) if token != "" -> application_url <> "/resume/" <> token
(with line 586: `let application_url =
                    origin_base <> "/apply/" <> vacancy.short_code` and line 36: `let origin_base = domain_helpers.build_origin_url(req, "")`) — contrast draft_handler.gleam: "emailed capability URLs come from vacancy.origin_domain — NEVER the request origin."
detail: The same PR that hardens the public continue-link email to vacancy.origin_domain ships a second path emailing the same 288-bit resume capability built from the request Host. Not exploitable here (Svix-signed webhook plus validate_origin_domain's project-hash allowlist), but the defense-in-depth rule the PR codifies is applied inconsistently.
recommended_fix: Build the stage-2 continue URL from vacancy.origin_domain (email_client.build_entity_url) like send_draft_continue_link does, keeping request origin only for dev/staging pass-through.

title: Draft-save ack is indistinguishable across persisted, cap-rejected, and tombstone-suppressed writes
detail: upsert_application_draft returns Ok with zero rows when the 500-per-vacancy cap rejects a brand-new pair (or the erased/submitted guard blocks the update); the handler answers ok:true either way, so a new applicant on a capped vacancy is told their answers saved when nothing persisted. Tombstone suppression warrants silence; cap rejection is a different case now conflated with it.
recommended_fix: Match on pog.Returned row count: keep ok:true for the guarded-row case, but consider ok:false (or a 'closed'-style flag) when a new pair was cap-rejected so the client isn't assured of a save that never happened.
